title: Round 10 / ECDLP-35: frontier exploration C — barrier inversion
question: Barrier inversion: enumerate every barrier the lab has proven or cataloged (generic-group, SLP/algebraic degree, transfer homomorphism, factor-base/index-calculus, cover, equidistribution), state each one's exact assumptions, characterize algorithm classes that violate ALL of them simultaneously, and propose + cheaply test the most concrete such class.

claims: T1 (experimental, toy, seed 1): lattice (Howgrave-Graham) decomposition of Semaev S_3 into interval-factor-base points reaches only box exponent alpha ~0.05-0.10 empirically (D<=5) and <=0.1585 analytically (D<=40, limit 1/6) for the tested lattice family; alpha>=0.45 succeeded 0/5 in every cell. Pre-registered kill met. Elementary cost law: boxes alpha<1/2 give total relation cost >= p^(1-alpha) > sqrt p.

T2 (experimental, p~2^19, 2 seeds): no Fourier line against group characters for smoothness/primality/squarefree/Liouville predicates of x (and amended symmetric y-smooth); positive control detected, negative control clean; nominal seed-1 hits (S1,S7 rank_p 0.04) did not replicate in seed 2. Pre-registered S4 had an invalid even-pair null and was amended post hoc (recorded).
Barrier map B1-B11 with exact assumptions (literature + lab HYPs); the common unconstrained resource is integer structure of coordinate representatives plus non-homomorphic maps.

B5 (proof sketch, UNREVIEWED, conditional on rational analogue HYP-6aef8c30): equality-branching algebraic decision trees satisfy N <= c*4^L, i.e. L >= (1/2)log2(N/c); order comparisons/bit tests not covered.
C2 (unreduced Miller/orbit-product cocycle) killed by derivation, not executed: pairing target F_p^*/(F_p^*)^r is trivial when gcd(r,p-1)=1. C4 (xedni) killed by literature, not re-run. C5 open.
Nothing here changes the status of the open target HYP-2de84d42 (unproved, no evidence for or against).
next_action: Prove the rational-function analogue (HYP-6aef8c30) to make B5 unconditional and study a comparison/bit-augmented decision-tree model; independently review the barrier tables before any write-up; drop lattice-decomposition and smoothness-spectrum routes unless a new lattice family beats alpha=1/2.
